nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression (GPR) model was trained at each voxel in the control cohort to predict cerebellar gray matter volume. 10-fold cross-validation was used in neurotypical individuals before retraining the model to make predictions in individuals with autism.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: A Gaussian process regression model was trained at each voxel in the control cohort using age, sex, site of inclusion, FSIQ, and intracranial volume (ICV) as covariates to predict cerebellar gray matter volume.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Laidi2022.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Normative Modeling

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cerebellar gray matter volume at each voxel was the response variable. Structural T1-weighted images were preprocessed with the SUIT pipeline which is specifically adapted to the cerebellum.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: A Gaussian process regression model was trained at each voxel in the control cohort using age, sex, site of inclusion, FSIQ, and intracranial volume (ICV) as covariates to predict cerebellar gray matter volume.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Laidi2022.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Normative Modeling

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Five explanatory variables were used in the normative model: age, sex, site of inclusion, Full Scale IQ (FSIQ), and intracranial volume (ICV). A secondary analysis was also conducted excluding FSIQ from the covariates.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: A Gaussian process regression model was trained at each voxel in the control cohort using age, sex, site of inclusion, FSIQ, and intracranial volume (ICV) as covariates to predict cerebellar gray matter volume. We ran a secondary analysis excluding FSIQ from the covariates.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Laidi2022.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Normative Modeling
